_comment_top: Annotated example config for nd-rating-sync. Fields with leading underscores are inline notes — they are ignored by the plugin. Copy the relevant pieces into the Plugin Settings UI in Navidrome (avatar → Plugins → nd-rating-sync). The schema and defaults live in manifest.json.
_comment_admin_scalars: Top-level admin-only settings. Apply globally; only Navidrome admins should change these.
_comment_libraries: One entry per Navidrome library. The libraryId is the internal ID shown on the Libraries admin page — NOT the display name. libraryName is purely for your own reference. Each library carries its own users[] list, so a single user can be configured differently in different libraries.

users._comment_alice: Alice keeps her library tagged with FMPS_Rating (written by MediaMonkey, Strawberry, Quod Libet, beets, etc.). She wants ratings she has already set inside Navidrome to win over file tags, so skip_already_rated stays true (the default). foobar2000 is listed as a fallback for the few albums she imported from a Windows machine — if a song has both FMPS_RATING and a plain RATING tag, FMPS_RATING wins because MediaMonkey is listed first.

users._comment_bob: Bob is a long-time foobar2000 user on Windows. His files have a plain RATING tag (1–5 integer), and some older albums have POPM frames written by WMP or iTunes. He wants every file's tag to overwrite whatever Navidrome currently shows, so skip_already_rated is false. clear_rating_if_untagged is also enabled so that songs he has removed ratings from in foobar2000 (tag absent or 0) will have their Navidrome rating cleared too — this requires skip_already_rated=false, otherwise already-rated songs would be skipped before the file is read. The first match in his tagOrder wins on a per-file basis.

libraries._comment_second_library: Optional second library example. Useful if you keep, say, lossy stream rips separate from your main lossless collection. Note that Bob is omitted here — he simply doesn't get rating sync for this library, while Alice still does.
